newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine local oil prices seen rising sharply.
newsitem.headline: Philippine local oil prices seen rising sharply.

text.p: Philippine petroleum product prices may rise on an average by as much as 60 centavos per litre as a weaker peso would mean higher crude import costs, an industry official said on Friday.

Considering an exchange rate of 29 pesos per dollar compared to the previous 26.4, the landed cost of crude will increase by 40 centavos per litre, the official from one of three oil companies in the country said.

"With roughly 20 billion litres a year consumption, this will cost the oil firms eight billion pesos, how can the industry absorb that? But we still have to see at what level the peso would stabilise," said the official.

The official said that on top of the increase in the landed cost of crude, foreign exchange losses of oil firms due to dollar-denominated debts will translate to about 20 centavos a litre increase in cost.
The peso plunged 11.5 percent to 29.45 per dollar on Friday before trades were suspended following the Central Bank's announcement that it will allow the peso to depreciate.
The Philippines oil refiners are Petron Corp, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp and Caltex (Philippines) Inc.
